nodes.title: The default-password CI gate catches one shape and calls it clean — 16 published passwords are exempt by design, and 4 of 5 canaries walk past it
nodes.description:
## The finding

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-default-passwords.sh` is a **live CI gate** (`pr-security-gates.yml:63`, `security-scan.yml:422`). It is far blinder than its name suggests, and the documented exemption is the *small* half.

## The exemption (known, by design)

Line 34 is `| grep -v 'seedPw(' \`. With **only that line deleted** (sha-asserted both ways and restored), the lint exits 1 with **16 flagged lines — sixteen other seeded accounts' published default passwords**, invisible to it by design.

## The blind spots (not by design)

Five canaries planted through the real script:

| plant | result |
| -- | -- |
| `services/`, `.ts`, ends `123` | **SEEN** — positive control, the instrument is live |
| `services/`, `.ts`, not ending `123` | MISSED — any other password shape |
| `frontend/`, `.ts`, ends `123` | MISSED — only `services/` and `packages/` are scanned |
| `services/`, `.sql`, ends `123` | MISSED — only `.ts/.tsx/.js`; **the seed SQL that** `fixtures.ts` **cites as source-of-truth is invisible** |
| `scripts/` subdir, `.ts`, ends `123` | MISSED — `--exclude-dir=scripts,tests,__tests__` |

So the gate catches exactly one shape — a `*123` literal, in a `.ts/.tsx/.js` file, under `services/` or `packages/`, not in an excluded directory, and not behind `seedPw(`.

## Why this is worth its own ticket

A guard with a documented exemption is a guard with a hole of a **known** size — and the hole never appears in the guard's own green result. This one passes today, passed before [KS-949](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-949), and would have passed with the real-person account and its published password still in place. It is a live gate that gives false assurance in CI.

- [ ] Widen the file-type and directory scope, or state the scope in the gate's own output so a green result says what it actually covered
- [ ] Decide whether the `seedPw(` exemption should survive at all now that one account (the platform admin) is held to a stricter rule than the lint enforces
- [ ] A password shape that is not `*123`

## Provenance

The exemption and the `docker-compose.yml:755` default were disclosed by the filer while doing KS-949 and **confirmed at source** by the tier-1 QA gate on PR #885 (2026-09-06T21:29:45Z); the 16-line count and the five canaries are the gate's measurement, not the filer's.

*Filed by s143 (seat A), 2026-09-07.*
